summary:
Six mappers plus my own verification in /Users/williamcory/flows-buildsys produce a plan of 19 lanes across 6 waves, with every lane owning a disjoint file set within its wave. I independently confirmed the load-bearing disputed claims by running the code, not by reading it.

THREE FINDINGS CHANGE THE PLAN MATERIALLY.

(1) The baseline is already red. `packages/targets/test/GeneratedRootFiles.test.ts` fails right now: its restated `allowBuilds` omits `playwright: false`, which BUILD.ts:65 declares and pnpm-workspace.yaml:14 carries. I ran it (packages/targets, vitest run test/GeneratedRootFiles.test.ts): "1 failed | 19 passed". The non-negotiable "existing gates stay green" is violated before any decision is implemented. Wave 0 fixes it.

(2) D13's premise is empirically false and hides a live correctness bug. I built a scratch workspace and ran the real CLI. `//pkg/src/internal:lib` resolves today — nested BUILD.ts is already label-addressable at arbitrary depth, and `//...` enumerates it. Worse: adding `pkg/src/internal/BUILD.ts` silently removed `pkg/src/internal/b.ts` from `//pkg:lib`'s declared inputs (verified by diffing `build //pkg:lib --plan --json`), while the parent's `tsc -b` still compiles that subtree. Bazel's subpackage pruning already exists in Input.ts:401-415/539/645. So D13's label layer is built, and D5's cache flip lands a stale-green hazard on top of it unless a plan-time guard lands first.

(3) D5 is licensed by a premise that is only half true, and its rule list is wrong in both directions. D5 claims D2 falsifies the Target.ts:496-499 comment. But the docs record a second, independent reason D2 does not touch (caching.md:112-114, ts-build.md:87: the executable toolchain is not complete key material — today the only toolchain material is one sha256 of pnpm-lock.yaml at Planner.ts:901). Measured: NINE rules fall through to the default (D5 names three), and SIXTEEN already declare `cache: false` (D5's opt-out list names nine and misses seven). Flipping without fixing declared-input completeness produces stale green test runs immediately: Vitest declares only `test/**/*.test.ts` plus `src/**/*.ts`, and 97 files under `packages/*/test/` (52 .ts harnesses, plus fixtures) are in neither.

ORDERING. Foundation first, as instructed, but the interlock is deeper than the brief assumes. D1 splits into an additive registry (Wave 1) and the attr removal across 20 rules (Wave 2), because the removal touches nearly every hot file and must not run beside anything. D12 is not one decision but a capability (lockfile parsing, Wave 1) plus a surface (npm targets, Wave 3) — and it is a hard prerequisite for D2, not a peer, because every catalog rule invokes its tool through `pnpm exec` and no target declares node_modules. D2 therefore lands as opt-in projection (Wave 2) and only becomes the default per rule as D12 completes each rule's input closure. D5 moves to Wave 4, behind the three prerequisites that actually gate it.

SHARP COLLISIONS RESOLVED. Four decisions want `packages/targets/src/Target.ts` (D5 cache, D6 visibility, D15 sandbox, D12 reservedRoots); it is owned by exactly one lane per wave and never two. `Planner.ts`, `Executor.ts`, `Workspace.ts`, `Smithers.ts`, and root `BUILD.ts` are each single-owner per wave. D4 is merged into the D1b rule-signature lane because both edit the same constructors. D7 moved out of Wave 2 because its root targets collide with D1b's root BUILD.ts.

CANNOT BE DONE AS SPECIFIED: 12 items, led by D2's `sandbox-exec` hint (deprecated, absent from this repo and the spec vault, which specifies copy-in projection instead), D10's changesets (no .changeset/, no dependency, nothing to wire), D10's NpmPublish (cannot execute — ExecIrreversibleLive is absent from Executor.ts:239-254 — and publishes a directory, which with source-first manifests would publish TypeScript), and D11's write mode (GithubCiGen models no `needs`, `permissions`, matrix, or step `if`, and drops all 60+ ci.yml comments).

Also: `//:ci` never runs in CI. Measured — GithubCiGen kinds are [build,lint]; ci.yml runs only the `docs` verb and `ci //packages/...`, and `query //packages/...` returns 272 labels with zero `//:` among them (280 total, 5 root). Landing D7 alone changes nothing operationally until a step plans it.

waves.rationale: Four foundation lanes with genuinely disjoint file sets. D1 is split so its additive half (the toolchain registry and WORKSPACE.ts discovery) lands here and its destructive half (removing the attr from 20 rules) lands in Wave 2; this is the only way D1 can share a wave with anything, because the removal touches nearly every hot file. The other three lanes create new files or touch files no other lane wants: the Rust genrule needs no toolchain attr (verified: ToolBuild.Attrs has no packageManager), the lockfile parser and the projection primitive are entirely new modules. All three de-risk large Wave 2 and Wave 3 lanes by proving their hardest mechanism first.

decisions: D1 (additive half): toolchain registry, WORKSPACE.ts, discovery, key material
lanes.task: Build the toolchain registry and teach discovery about WORKSPACE.ts, WITHOUT removing any target attr. Every rule keeps its `packageManager` attr through this wave; W2-A removes them. (1) Add `registerToolchains({runtime, packageManager})` plus a pure accessor to packages/targets/src/PackageManager.ts and the runtime half to Runtime.ts. The registry must perform no I/O — packages/targets/src/PackageManager.ts:5-7 states BUILD.ts evaluation is side-effect free and that property is load-bearing for the read-only CLI contract. Reject double registration with a message naming both call sites. Reject a read before registration rather than returning a default. (2) Export `registerToolchains` from packages/targets/src/Smithers.ts beside the existing `Runtime` (:191) and `PackageManager` (:213) namespaces; packages/targets/test/Smithers.test.ts:12-20 asserts the barrel's keys equal this module's keys, so this is the only legal export site. (3) Create /Users/williamcory/flows-buildsys/WORKSPACE.ts calling `registerToolchains` with the runtime and packageManager values currently at BUILD.ts:24 and BUILD.ts:30. Do not move PnpmWorkspace, Lockfile, Install, or the Secret declarations yet — that is W2-A, and moving them here would delete the labels `//:workspace`, `//:lockfile`, and `//:nodeModules` mid-wave. (4) Teach discovery WORKSPACE.ts: `buildEntry(canonical, "BUILD.ts")` is called at Workspace.ts:477 (resolveConfig) and :514 (resolveRemoteCache); add a WORKSPACE.ts pass with declared precedence over the root BUILD.ts, and a namespace scan for the toolchain registration mirroring `declaredConfig` (:440-446) and `declaredRemoteCache` (:448-454). Note the memoization at Workspace.ts:349/:372-376 keyed on canonical path plus SHA-256 of file bytes: the two resolvers already share one evaluation, and WORKSPACE.ts must join the same memo. Both resolvers run in Cli.prepare BEFORE Workspace.make, so WORKSPACE.ts must be resolvable without the workspace index. (5) Extend `isBuildModule` in effect-resolution.js:34-38, which today tests `pathname.endsWith("/BUILD.ts")`, so a WORKSPACE.ts reached by a relative import from a BUILD.ts keeps the ESM format override instead of falling through to tsx's CommonJS bridge. (6) CRITICAL, do not skip: fold the registered toolchain into `ambient` at Planner.ts:897-906. Target attrs are key material (serialized at Planner.ts:960 via `attrsValue`), and the whole `{_tag:"PackageManager", name, version, executable, runtime}` value currently rides there. When W2-A removes the attr, the toolchain leaves every target's key unless ambient carries it. Land the ambient addition NOW, in the same wave as the registry, so the removal in W2-A is key-neutral rather than a silent regression. Also repoint `layers()` at Planner.ts:812-833, which derives the Install/Lockfile layer identity from `attrs.packageManager.name@version` and would return `[]` after the removal. (7) `declaredToolchain` at engine.ts:234-264 reads `attrs.packageManager` and silently falls back to `defaultToolchain` (pnpm `>=0.0.0`); give it the registry as its source with the attr as a fallback during this wave. (8) `smthrs install` never applies the declared toolchain: Cli.ts:230-241 calls `runInstall` with no `toolchain`, and engine.ts:402-430 accepts an optional one. Pass the registered toolchain. Treat this as a wire to BUILD, not one to preserve.

decisions: D12 (capability half): the lockfile becomes readable
lanes.task: Nothing in this repository parses pnpm-lock.yaml. It is only digested, in two places: Planner.ts:901 folds `Input.digestFile(root/pnpm-lock.yaml)` into ambient, and PackageManager.ts:1412-1430 digests it for the measure action under a 64 MiB bound. D12 cannot address individual npm packages without reading the file, so this lane builds that capability and nothing else. Write a targeted scanner for the pnpm 9.x lockfile format that yields, per package, its name, version, resolution integrity, and its dependency edges. Do NOT add a YAML dependency: packages/targets/src/GithubWorkflow.ts:18-26 records that a YAML dependency was rejected on dependency-policy grounds and that a hand-written targeted scanner is the house precedent; follow it, and cite it in the module JSDoc. Bound the read the way PackageManager.ts already does (`maximumLockfileBytes`, :202) rather than reading unbounded — the file is 839 KB today. Mirror reference/effect conventions: `make`/`makeNoop`/`layer`/`layerNoop`, `@since`/`@category` JSDoc, errors as tagged classes. Export nothing from Smithers.ts in this wave — this is an internal capability with no authoring surface yet; W3-C adds the surface. Keep the parser total: an unrecognized lockfile version must fail with a named error, never parse partially.
lanes.tests: New packages/build/test/PnpmLock.test.ts. Parse the repository's own pnpm-lock.yaml (839 KB, real input, no fixture) and assert a plausible package count and that a known entry such as `effect` resolves with a version and integrity. Add negative cases: an unsupported lockfileVersion, a truncated file, and a file over the size bound, each producing the named error rather than a partial parse. Add a determinism case: parsing twice yields structurally identical output.
lanes.verification: Run the packages/build vitest suite. Confirm no other package's behaviour changed: `node packages/build-cli/src/main.js query '//...'` still returns the same label set. Note for the reviewer that adding a source file under packages/build changes `implementationFingerprint` (Planner.ts:697-737 digests 14 loaded source trees) and therefore invalidates every stored cache entry once; this is expected and benign, and Planner.test.ts's fingerprint suite is sensitive to it.

decisions: D2 (capability half): confined projection of a declared file set
lanes.task: Build the primitive D2 needs, as a new sibling module, before touching Exec.ts. Do NOT edit SafeFs.ts: its `Io` seam is deliberately read-only (`realpath`, `lstat`, `readdir`, `open` only, SafeFs.ts:109-114) and adding write capability to a read boundary is the wrong shape under the effect-repo conventions this repo mirrors. Project.ts takes a workspace root, a scratch root, and a list of workspace-relative file paths, and materializes exactly those files under the scratch root, creating parent directories as needed. Reuse SafeFs's confinement discipline rather than reinventing it: `canonicalRoot` and `inside` for containment on canonical paths (SafeFs.ts:220-238), `resolveFile`'s refusal of a symlink whose resolution leaves the root (:328-391), and `withOpen`'s post-open re-verification of the descriptor's own fstat, size, mtime, ctime, and canonical location (:481-540). Copy the confined-write shape from GeneratedFile.ts:279-376 (mkdir, O_EXCL O_NOFOLLOW sibling temp, write, fsync, re-check parent dev:ino, rename, fsync the directory). Prefer hardlink with copy fallback for size, but hardlinking must never let the child mutate the workspace original — if the platform cannot guarantee that, copy. Also provide the reverse operation: collect a declared output set from the scratch root back into the workspace, under the same confinement. Read packages/engine-store/src/WorkspaceSandbox.ts:1137-1165 and :1261-1294 first — it is this repository's own prior art for exactly this transaction (seed a base map from the declared read set, diff the whole map at settlement, copy back under symlink-resolving confinement) and its module doc at :1-38 states plainly that it is a determinism model and NOT a security boundary, and that a spawned native process sits outside it. Say the same thing in this module's doc. Export nothing from Smithers.ts.
lanes.tests: New packages/targets/test/Project.test.ts. Cover: a projected file is readable at the scratch root; an undeclared sibling is absent; a symlinked source is refused rather than followed; a path escaping the root lexically or through a symlink is refused; a projected tree round-trips through the collect direction; concurrent projection into two scratch roots does not interfere; and projection of a file that changes on disk mid-projection is detected rather than silently torn. Add the adversarial cases the house style expects: a path with a `..` segment, an absolute path, and a path resolving into `.git` or `.flows`.
lanes.verification: Run the packages/targets vitest suite; it must be green including the new file. Confirm nothing else changed behaviour: `node packages/build-cli/src/main.js query '//...'` returns the same labels, and `packages/targets/test/Smithers.test.ts` still passes (proving the new module is not exported from the authoring namespace). Reviewer should read the module doc and confirm it states the same limitation WorkspaceSandbox.ts:1-38 states — that this is a determinism boundary, not a security boundary — because the honest scope of D2 depends on that being written down.

D4: rules take an inline constructor or a config-file path
lanes.task: Remove the toolchain from target attrs and add D4's path form, in one pass, because both edit the same constructors. (1) Drop the `packageManager` attr from the 20 rules that carry it — measured exactly: BiomeCheck:25, Changesets:58, DepsLint:28, Dprint:26, DtsBuild:26, EsLint:24, GithubCiGen:351, Install:40, JsrPublish:23, Lockfile:37, NpmPublish:23, PackageLint:25, PnpmWorkspaceFile:33, SortPackageJson:25, TsBuild:26, Typecheck:23, TypedocDocs:23, Vitest:24, VitestCoverage:27, VitestWatch:24 — and the bare `runtime` attr from Clean:24 and DepsLint:27. Each rule's implementation reads the registry W1-A built instead. DepsLint is the only rule carrying both. (2) Drop `Options.packageManager` from StandardPackage.ts:32 and its five pass-throughs (:102, :114, :123, :133, :142). This is what makes package BUILD.ts files toolchain-free. Note StandardPackage.ts:96-99 already defaults the jsdoc lint config to `Input.file("//eslint.jsdoc.js")`, so the three BUILD.ts files importing `rootJSDocConfig` are restating the default and can simply drop the import — D1's claim that this form 'already works' is confirmed. (3) Move PnpmWorkspace (BUILD.ts:53-80), Lockfile (:107-110), Install (:116-120), and the two Secret declarations (:43-46) from root BUILD.ts into WORKSPACE.ts. CRITICAL CONSEQUENCE: this deletes the labels `//:workspace`, `//:lockfile`, and `//:nodeModules` unless the workspace index registers WORKSPACE.ts exports as targets in the root package. `nodeModules` is also the second entry in the hardcoded default-target candidate list at Workspace.ts:992-999, so a bare `//` stops resolving. Decide explicitly and implement one of two options: register WORKSPACE.ts exports into the root package so the labels survive, or move only the toolchain and Secret declarations and leave the three targets in BUILD.ts. Recommendation: register them, because packages/build/docs/getting-started/first-build.md:27 and :92 teach `//:nodeModules` and `//` resolving to it. Whichever you choose, say so in the commit message and update the docs in the same change. (4) Delete the `import { packageManager } from "../../BUILD.ts"` line from all six package BUILD.ts files: build-cli:12, build:16, engine:9, flow:10, plan:7, targets:12, plus the `rootJSDocConfig` import in build-cli, flow, and targets. packages/engine/BUILD.ts:22-23 is the special case — it threads `runtime: packageManager.runtime` by reaching through the manager declaration and must read the registry for both halves. Keep the cross-package `import { lib as flow } from "../flow/BUILD.ts"` edges: they are the mechanism D13's folder units will reuse. Note packages/plan/BUILD.ts becomes a bare `StandardPackage({deps: [], cwd})` and is arguably deletable — do NOT delete it in this lane, because packages/build-cli/test/CommittedBuildFiles.test.ts:35-53 names it explicitly; deleting it is a separate decision. (5) Fix two stale comments that will misdirect future work: packages/build-cli/BUILD.ts:4-5 and packages/targets/BUILD.ts:4-5 both claim 'its tsconfig sets noEmit'. Neither tsconfig sets noEmit; both set outDir dist/esm with declaration true. The real reason those two use Typecheck instead of TsBuild is `"private": true` and no build script. (6) D4: add the path form to the rules that have a real tool config file — Vitest, VitestWatch, VitestCoverage, EsLint, Dprint, BiomeCheck, Typecheck, TsBuild. The definition returned by Target.make is `(attrsInput) => ...` and validates through `options.attrs.make` (Target.ts:698), so the path form is a normalization step before `.make`, not a schema change. HARD CONSTRAINT, do not violate it: the path form must still produce a COMPLETE declared-input set, derived from the same conventions StandardPackage uses, never an empty or omitted one. `Vitest("vitest.config.ts")` must expand to the same `tests`/`sources` declarations `StandardPackage` would supply, plus the named config file. A path form that omits declared inputs is actively dangerous under D2's projection and D5's cache flip, and the config file is not parsed — the build system does not read vitest's `include` patterns. Document that limitation in each rule's JSDoc rather than pretending the path form derives the globs.

lanes.task: Land input-projected execution as OPT-IN, defaulting OFF for every existing rule. decisions: D6 (enforcement half): plan-time visibility
D13 (correctness guard): nested BUILD.ts must not silently prune a parent's inputs
lanes.task: Two jobs that share the planner and must not be split across lanes. (1) D6 enforcement. Its premise is FALSE: there is no root `scripts/circular.mjs`. `ls scripts/` returns browser-check, check-test-pins, flows-backup, pack-release, release-rehearsal, set-release-version, smoke-release only. What exists is 45 identical per-package copies at `packages/*/scripts/circular.mjs`, each ~18 lines calling madge over that one package's `src` with `skipTypeImports: true`. There is no repo-wide import graph, no cross-package edge, no type-only import coverage, and no mapping from an import specifier to a target label. Build the walker: new packages/build-cli/src/Imports.ts resolving each source file's imports to a target label. Enforce at plan time inside `visit` (Planner.ts:917-985), which is where dependency edges already resolve to labels. Use `packagePathOf` (Workspace.ts:1187-1192) and `inputPackagePathOf` (:1195-1208) as the package-identity resolvers — and note `packagePathOf` prefers the registered label over `Metadata.sourceFile`, which matters because synthesized targets take the macro path, so `sourceSite()` (Target.ts:570-590) finds no BUILD.ts frame and `Metadata.sourceFile` is undefined for all 39 synthesized packages. Never resolve a declaring folder through `Metadata.sourceFile`. Implement `Visibility.group({where})`'s manifest query here, reading `smthrs.group` from each package manifest — nothing in the build system reads that field today. (2) D13's correctness guard, which I verified empirically and which is the more urgent half. In a scratch workspace running the real CLI, adding `pkg/src/internal/BUILD.ts` removed `pkg/src/internal/b.ts` from `//pkg:lib`'s declared inputs while the parent's `tsc -b` still compiles that subtree. The pruning is deliberate and already implemented — `walk` refuses to descend into any directory holding a BUILD.ts (Input.ts:539), `crossesPackageBoundary` refuses a static prefix reaching past a subpackage marker (:474-491, :645), `isPackage` compares the basename exactly (:401-415) — but nothing notices that the parent's tool still reads the pruned files. Add a plan-time check: when a target's declared glob is pruned by a subpackage boundary, the target must depend on a target in that subpackage, or the plan fails with a message naming both. This must land BEFORE Wave 4's cache flip; without it, editing a file under a new folder unit replays a stale green parent build. Also make `defaultRules` order deterministic (Workspace.ts:935-939): it is currently BUILD.ts LOAD order, not declaration order, so 'first eligible wins' is invocation-dependent in any workspace with overlapping PackageDefaults declarations.

Add it to `executionOptions` (Cli.ts:29-33) and `ExecutionFlags` (:52-56) and forward it from `runVerb` (:147-157) and `runCi` (:197-206) into `Executor.execute`. (3) Read the per-target `sandbox` field W2-C added, from planned metadata rather than from attrs at execution time, for the same reason `declaredOutputs` is read that way (Executor.ts:781-790). (4) D15's hard invariant: an un-sandboxed target is STILL CACHED. Do not touch the cache guards at Executor.ts:928 and :1003. Execution flags are already excluded from key material by precedent — `readCache` and `remoteCache` are executor options and never reach the planner (Executor.ts:103-118) — so the flag follows that precedent. But the sandbox MODE must be key material so a target run once un-sandboxed and once sandboxed does not share an entry; the planner is owned by another lane this wave, so file the contract: mode belongs in `capabilities()` (Planner.ts:835-842), which is the existing per-target capability list and already defaults to `["fs:read","proc:spawn"]`. decisions: D12 (surface half): every npm package is a target
lanes.task: Make individual npm packages addressable, using W1-C's parser. D12 is blocked by three independent, deliberate safety mechanisms and by a manager that cannot do it; the decision names none of them. Read all four before designing. (a) Declared-input expansion cannot see node_modules at all: `walk` skips any entry named `node_modules` or `.git` (Input.ts:544) and `expandGlob` returns empty for any pattern whose static prefix contains a node_modules segment (:625). (b) Declared-output capture refuses symbolic links at the declared root and anywhere inside the captured tree (ToolBuild.ts:657-662, :761-763), and pnpm's node_modules is a symlink farm. (c) Nothing may declare an output under the cache directory: `reservedRoots` is `{.flows, .git}` (Target.ts:99) and the store lives at `.flows/store` (build/src/PackageManager.ts:170-180). (d) Only pnpm has an implementation — `makeNpm`, `makeBun`, and yarn all return `makeNoop`, which fails every operation with code `unsupported` (build/src/PackageManager.ts:973-993, :1099-1120, :1135-1177). RECOMMENDED DESIGN, chosen to avoid relaxing any of the three safety properties: make `npm("effect")` a lockfile-derived HANDLE, not a file set. Add a new `Input.Declared` member keyed on the lockfile entry — name, version, integrity — rather than on files under node_modules. Its digest comes from the lockfile entry plus the transitive closure the W1-C parser resolves, so it is content-addressed without reading the installed tree, without touching the node_modules guards, without needing symlinked outputs, and without relaxing reservedRoots. Do NOT relax guards (a), (b), or (c): each has a written rationale and relaxing any of them is a redesign of a safety property, not a feature. `Input.Declared` is a three-member union today — `Glob {pattern, exclude[]}`, `File {path}`, `GitDiff {base}` (Input.ts:26-89) — so this is a fourth member and every consumer of the union must handle it. Add packages/targets/src/NpmLock.ts providing `NpmLock({lockfile})` and the `npm(name)` accessor. NOTE the D12 example in DECISIONS.md still threads `packageManager` into `Smithers.NpmLock({packageManager, lockfile})` while D1 states no target attr threads it any more; the two decisions contradict each other. Resolve it by reading the registry: `NpmLock({lockfile})`. Export both from Smithers.ts, and declare the workspace's `npm` in WORKSPACE.ts — except WORKSPACE.ts is owned by another lane in Wave 2 and free in Wave 3, so you own it here only if no Wave 3 lane also claims it; it does not, so add the declaration. Confirm and preserve `Install`'s two independent reasons for not caching (packages/targets/src/Install.ts:110 and the flow-level admission rule at build/src/Install.ts:12-30, where every action uses `boundaryMode: "expected"` and admission requires sealed + hard); D12 changes what Install produces, not whether it replays.

Add a Planner-adjacent assertion (without editing Planner) that a target depending on `npm("effect")` re-keys when the lockfile entry changes but not when an unrelated entry changes — this is the whole point of the decision and is what the single coarse `ambient.lockfile` digest cannot do today.

decisions: D10 (targets half): NpmPublish wired into the package macro
lanes.task: Make `//packages/journal:publish` exist. Three gaps block a naive wiring; fix all three or the target is a green-looking graph that cannot publish. (1) THE MACRO HAS NO MANIFEST. `StandardPackage.Options` (:26-44) carries no name, no version, and no group, and `PackageDefaults.expand` (:236-256) calls the macro with only `{cwd, ...declaredAttrs}` where attrs is ONE static record shared by every match. So the macro cannot decide engine-vs-agent membership, cannot know the dist tag, and cannot name the package. Teach `PackageDefaults.expand` to read the matched directory's manifest and pass name, version, and `smthrs.group` alongside `cwd`. This is the same per-directory manifest query D6's `Visibility.group` needs; that lane builds the reader for the planner, so reuse rather than duplicate — coordinate the shared helper's location with W3-A. (2) NPMPUBLISH PUBLISHES A DIRECTORY, NOT A TARBALL. Its argv is `pnpm publish --registry R --access A --tag T --no-git-checks [--dry-run]` run in `dirname(packageJson.path)` (:43-46, :77-91), while release.yml:167 publishes a tarball path. With this repo's source-first manifests (`exports: ".": "./src/index.ts"`, confirmed in packages/journal/package.json), running NpmPublish as written on a real package would publish TypeScript source as the package entry — exactly the bug scripts/pack-release.mjs's staging copy exists to prevent (its `publicationManifest` at :137-151 lifts `publishConfig.exports` into `exports` before packing). Add a tarball input or a staged-directory input; do not publish the working directory. (3) NO IDEMPOTENCE PROBE. release.yml:161-168 skips an already-published spec via `pnpm view <spec> version` because npm versions are immutable; a rerun of `//packages/x:publish` would hard-fail without it. (4) Reconcile provenance: NpmPublish rides `npm_config_provenance` env only (:90) while release.yml passes `--provenance` on argv; pick one. (5) `verbGate: ["run"]` (:75) is enforced by the planner (`assertVerbGate`, Planner.ts:877-884) and refuses the target when a build/test/lint/docs graph reaches it, INCLUDING transitively — so adding `publish` to StandardPackage's returned record does not poison `smthrs ci`. Verify that transitively, not just for a directly named target. (6) JsrPublish additionally requires a `jsr.json`/`deno.json` per package and none exists in this repo; wire it behind the same gate or leave it declared-and-unwired and say so in its JSDoc. (7) Changesets: do NOT adopt it in this lane. There is no `.changeset/` directory, no `@changesets/*` in any manifest or in pnpm-lock.yaml, no config, and no CHANGELOG — verified. The rule shells out to `pnpm exec changeset version` and has zero call sites. Leave it alone; Wave 5 decides.

Do not publish anything in a test — assert the plan and the argv, not the effect.

decisions: D5 (hard prerequisite): the cache must restore outputs, not just record that they existed
lanes.task: The build cache is an action cache with no content-addressed store behind it, so a cache hit cannot reproduce a single output file. Verified: CachedResult is {key,target,label,exitOk,output,storedAt} with output being a JSON success value (Cache.ts:31-38), and ToolBuild.captureOutputs DIGESTS each declared output into that payload (ToolBuild.ts:1044-1049) rather than storing bytes. @smthrs/artifacts is not a dependency of @smthrs/build-cli. Flipping cache to true (W4-A) on this substrate is worse than not caching: a hit on a clean tree marks TsBuild successful while dist/ does not exist. Wire the CAS. Add @smthrs/artifacts as a dependency and use its ArtifactStore: on a successful execution, store each declared output blob keyed by the digest captureOutputs already computes; on a cache hit, restore every declared output to its declared path before reporting success, and treat a missing blob as a MISS rather than a hit. packages/build/infra already serves /ac and /cas over HTTP, and RemoteArtifacts plus CombinedArtifacts already implement local-first/remote-second composition, so use them rather than writing a second client. A target that declares no outputs (a pure check such as Typecheck, EsLint, Dprint, Vitest) needs no blob and its existing envelope is sufficient; be explicit about that split.
lanes.tests: Round-trip: execute a ToolBuild target with a declared output, clear the workspace output path, re-run, and assert the file is restored byte-identically from cache. Miss-on-missing-blob: store an entry, delete the blob, assert the lookup reports a miss and re-executes. No-output targets: assert a check-only target still hits without touching the artifact store.
lanes.verification: From packages/build-cli run the vitest suite. Then end to end in the worktree: build a real target with outputs, record the output digest, rm -rf the output dir, build again, and confirm the file returns without the tool running (the executor must report a cache hit, not a re-execution).

waves.rationale: The cache flip lands only now, behind the three prerequisites that actually gate it: toolchain identity in key material (Wave 1), the subpackage pruning guard (Wave 3), and declared-input completeness (this lane). CI generation and dependency self-update run beside it on disjoint files.

decisions: D5: cache true by default, opt out by exception
lanes.task: Flip the default, but fix the prerequisite first. (1) PREREQUISITE, do this before touching Target.ts. Vitest declares only `tests: test/**/*.test.ts` and `sources: src/**/*.ts` (StandardPackage.ts:90, :122-131). Measured: 97 files live under `packages/*/test/` that are neither — 52 `.ts` harnesses such as packages/flow/test/MemoryFlowRuntime.ts and packages/engine/test/DurableLogEngine.ts, plus 45 fixtures in .sse, .cjs, .mjs, .mdx, .md, .js, .json, .tsx, .jsonl, .html. None is a declared input of any `:test` target, and the `deps: [lib]` edge does not cover them because lib's key is built from `src/**/*.ts`. Note that `check` and `fmt` already declare `Input.glob("test/**/*.ts")` (StandardPackage.ts:115, :141) and `test` does not — the asymmetry is the bug. Widen Vitest's declaration to cover the whole test directory, including non-.ts fixtures, before the flip. Without this, editing a harness replays a green test result. (2) Flip BOTH sites in Target.ts: `options.cache ?? false` at :687 inside `implementationDigest` and at :715 in `cacheableFor`. Flipping only :715 leaves the digest recording `["constant", false]` for a rule that is now cacheable, so the digest no longer identifies the cache decision it claims to identify. Flipping both changes `implementationDigest` for the nine affected rules, a one-time global invalidation of their stored entries — benign, but name it in the commit so it does not read as a durable-key regression to the LlmLint durableIdentityGuard target in lint/BUILD.ts. (3) Rewrite the JSDoc at Target.ts:494-501. Its stated reason — 'arbitrary target bodies can consult tools, services, or host state that attrs and declared inputs do not identify' — is what D5 quotes. Replace it with the true post-Wave-3 position rather than deleting it. (4) SCOPE CORRECTION, measured, and D5 is wrong in both directions. NINE rules fall through to the default, not three: BiomeCheck:106, DepsLint:104, DtsBuild:88, PackageLint:80, TsBuild:81, Typecheck:78, TypedocDocs:62, Vitest:57, VitestCoverage:89. SIXTEEN already declare `cache: false`, not nine: Changesets:102, Clean:80, Dev:53, Dprint:61, EsLint:72, Install:110, JsrPublish:69, LlmLint:1344, Lockfile:96, NewPackage:453, NpmPublish:74, PackageJson:1136, PnpmWorkspaceFile:140, SortPackageJson:63, Tsconfig:131, VitestWatch:63. D5's list omits Dprint, EsLint, LlmLint, SortPackageJson, PackageJsonWrite, Tsconfig, and VitestWatch — all already explicit and all unaffected by the flip. Do NOT delete an explicit `cache: false` because D5's list does not mention it. (5) SCOPE THE FLIP BY VALUE. Cache hits never restore artifacts: `CachedResult` (Cache.ts:32-51) holds only a JSON success envelope, and `checkDeclaredOutputs` re-measures the tree with a mismatch silently falling through to a run (Executor.ts:943-964). So flipping TsBuild, DtsBuild, and TypedocDocs buys nothing on a fresh CI checkout — no dist exists, so every build misses. The real wall-clock win is Typecheck, Vitest, VitestCoverage, BiomeCheck, DepsLint, and PackageLint, none of which declares outputs. Flip all nine but justify the change by those six, and record the artifact-store gap as the reason the other three are inert. (6) All nine have JSON-round-trippable success schemas, so the flip is encode-safe: Exec.Result is `{exitCode, stdout, stderr}` with timing deliberately excluded (Exec.ts:147-151), BiomeReport is two nullable Exec.Results, CoverageReport is an Exec.Result plus a string, and the build rules use `Outputs`. (7) Docs: caching.md:97-114 states 'non-cacheable by default', gives the four-row cacheability table, AND states the second justification D5 does not address — that external compiler, test, and lint targets remain non-cacheable until their executable and runtime toolchain are represented in the content key. Wave 1 fixed the declared toolchain half of that; the installed-binary half is still open, so say what is now true rather than deleting the caveat. reference/targets/README.md:30-40 states `Cacheable: Never` for four rules; ts-build.md:87, vitest.md:63, and typecheck.md:71 each carry the same one-line claim; concepts/targets.md:61 says cacheable resolves 'defaulting to false'.
lanes.tests: packages/targets/test/Target.test.ts:57-59 asserts `defaults arbitrary target implementations to non-cacheable` and inverts; :61-69 asserts explicit opt-in and must be rewritten as explicit opt-OUT. Add a test enumerating the catalog and asserting the exact cacheable set, so a future rule cannot silently join or leave it. Add the stale-replay regression test: run a `:test` target to a hit, edit a test HARNESS file (not a `.test.ts`), and assert the next run is a MISS — this is the guard for step 1 and the most important test in the lane. Confirm TypedFileAttrs.test.ts's `metadata.cacheable === false` assertion for Install still passes, proving the flip did not drag an opt-out along.
lanes.verification: `build '//packages/plan:check'` twice: second run reports a hit where it previously always ran. Then touch packages/plan/test/ any helper and confirm a miss. Then run the full `ci '//packages/...'` twice and confirm the second is substantially faster with no failures — and critically, that it is not faster because it is skipping work it should redo. Reviewer counts the cacheable rules and confirms nine changed and sixteen explicit opt-outs are untouched.

decisions: D7: the hand-written ci.yml gates become root targets
D11 (second half): GithubCiGen generates as well as checks
lanes.task: Model the gates and tighten the contract — but do NOT flip GithubCiGen to write mode; see the blocked item. (1) D7's seven gates are all real and all unmodelled (ci.yml:52, :57, :59, :65, :71, :75, :80), but seven is not the total. ci.yml has 69 steps; 8 map to graph targets and 61 do not; distinct unmodelled gate commands number 20 `run:` plus 3 gate-carrying `uses:`. `pnpm run browser` appears TWICE (:57 in job `test` and :237 as the whole `browser` job), so modelling it retires two steps and one job. Declare the seven as ToolBuild genrules exported from root BUILD.ts, following D8's precedent rather than writing three new rules — this keeps the authoring namespace unchanged and avoids a Smithers.ts edit. Their declared inputs must be complete, which matters now that Wave 4 flipped the default: scripts/pack-release.test.mjs reads BOTH workflow files and every `packages/*/package.json`, and scripts/set-release-version.test.mjs:59-63 reads every manifest live. Declaring these cacheable without that closure produces stale replays of exactly the gate meant to catch manifest drift. (2) `//:circular` is coarse and must be honest: `pnpm run circular` is `pnpm --recursive --if-present run circular` over 45 per-package copies of `scripts/circular.mjs`; there is no root script. Either declare a single root ToolBuild wrapping the recursive command and say in its JSDoc that it is package-granular underneath, or declare 45 per-package targets. Recommend the former for this wave. (3) THE GATE THAT NEVER RUNS. `//:ci` is never executed by any CI step — GithubCiGen's kinds are `["build","lint"]` (:895), ci.yml:50 runs the `docs` verb, and ci.yml:297 runs `ci "//packages/..."`, whose pattern excludes every `//:` root target. Verified: `query '//packages/...'` returns 272 labels with zero `//:` among them, against 280 total. So the contract mode D7 is meant to unblock has been inert since it was written. Add a CI step that actually plans `//:ci`, or D7 changes nothing operationally. This is the highest-value single line in the lane. (4) Tighten the contract instead of generating: `//:ci` declares ONE gate and ZERO requiredJobs today (BUILD.ts:135-141), so contract mode proves only that some unconditional step of job `test` runs `pnpm exec smthrs docs '//...'`. Add a gate entry per surviving hand-written command and a `requiredJobs` list naming test, rust, wasm-repro, bun, browser. Contract mode verifies exactly two things — every declared Gate runs in an unconditional step of an unconditional job, and every declared requiredJob exists and runs unconditionally (:254-269) — and deliberately IGNORES `continue-on-error` (GithubWorkflow.ts:1049-1055), so an advisory lane satisfies a gate. Keep that; it is documented and intentional. (5) HIDDEN COUPLING, do not miss this: scripts/pack-release.test.mjs:152-157 is a cross-workflow parity gate whose extractor (:24-31) recognises only `pnpm run <script>`, `pnpm test`, and `node [--test ]scripts/*.mjs`. The moment a ci.yml gate becomes a `smthrs` invocation, this test passes VACUOUSLY and silently stops protecting release.yml. Rewrite it in this same change to compare the two workflows' TARGET sets rather than their shell strings. (6) Convert PnpmWorkspaceFile to the Wave 2 shared GeneratedFile mode and the check/write pair — it was deferred from W2-D because another lane owned the file. (7) Fix ci.yml's stale shadow-lane comment at :267-269 claiming '130 targets over 26 packages'; measured, it is 271 roots over 45 packages. (8) Reconcile CONTRIBUTING.md:5-15, which lists two gates ci.yml never runs (`pnpm run test:examples`, `pnpm exec vocs build`) — state explicitly whether they are contract or local-only. (9) Note but do not fix: ci.yml:19 actionlints three workflows (ci, release, apps-deploy) while release.yml:49 lints two, despite ci.yml:14-15 claiming lockstep.
lanes.tests: Extend packages/targets/test/GithubWorkflow.test.ts (1721 lines; the golden render fixture at :1064-1160 is a byte-exact pin of `render`'s output, so any Job/Step schema field changes it). Add: the expanded gate list is proven against the checked-in ci.yml; a gate removed from ci.yml fails the contract; a required job made conditional fails; an advisory `continue-on-error` job still satisfies a gate. Rewrite scripts/pack-release.test.mjs's parity gate as a target-set comparison and add a case proving it FAILS when a gate exists in ci.yml but not release.yml — the current version would pass vacuously.
lanes.verification: `query '//...'` shows `//:browser`, `//:circular`, and the five `node --test` targets. `smthrs lint '//:ci'` now runs and PASSES against the checked-in ci.yml — and, decisively, fails if you delete any gate line from ci.yml and rerun. decisions: D14: BUILD.ts dep lists self-update in dev, are checked in CI
lanes.task: Maintain the dependency section of a BUILD.ts from real imports, with the same write|check duality D11 applies to generated files. Build on W3-A's packages/build-cli/src/Imports.ts — import it, do not fork it, and do not edit it (it is owned by that lane's wave and must stay single-source). D14 is the decision that actually deletes BUILD.ts files, not D1: `PackageDefaults` passes ONE static attrs record to every match (PackageDefaults.ts:236-240), so all 39 synthesized packages get an empty `deps` list and no dependency edges even when their package.json names workspace siblings — documented at packages/build/docs/extending/default-rules.md:104-124, and it is precisely why packages/engine/BUILD.ts and packages/flow/BUILD.ts exist at all (their only irreducible content is `deps: [flow]` and `deps: [plan]`). Write mode rewrites only the dependency section of a BUILD.ts, preserving everything else byte-for-byte including comments — this is a surgical edit, not a regeneration, and a full render would destroy the hand-written rationale in those files. Check mode fails on drift and mutates nothing. Gate write mode behind `NODE_ENV=production` and a strict flag as D14 specifies: strict and production are check-only. Reuse GeneratedFile's atomic publication path for the write half rather than writing a second one. Do not wire this into any BUILD.ts or into ci.yml in this lane; land the mechanism and its tests, and let a later change adopt it once it has run against the real tree without surprises.
lanes.tests: New packages/build-cli/test/DepSync.test.ts: check mode reports drift when a source file imports a sibling package the BUILD.ts does not list; write mode adds exactly that edge and leaves comments, formatting, and every other declaration byte-identical; write mode is refused under NODE_ENV=production and under the strict flag; a BUILD.ts with no dependency section is handled without corrupting it; a type-only import is handled per the declared policy (note the 45 per-package circular.mjs copies use `skipTypeImports: true`, so state and test whichever policy you choose). Include a round-trip case: write, then check, must report no drift.
lanes.verification: Run check mode against the real workspace and report what it finds without changing anything — expect it to flag the synthesized packages that have real sibling imports and empty dep lists, which is the D14 gap made visible for the first time. Confirm `query '//...'` is unchanged and no BUILD.ts on disk was modified by the test run. Both vitest suites green.

decisions: D10 (manifest and versioning half): DRY generated manifests, changeset-style versioning, internal range retargeting
lanes.task: Make published manifests generated and DRY without destroying the 45 hand-written ones. (1) THE REGRESSION RISK IS THE WHOLE LANE. No package.json is generated anywhere in flows today — the root `packageDefaults` macro is bare `StandardPackage` (BUILD.ts:145), which returns six targets and no manifest declaration; the only manifest-producing macro is in packages/build/BUILD.ts:51-67 and its glob anchors to `packages/build/packages/*`, matching nothing. So D10 starts from an unexercised code path. Adopting that macro at the root as written would rewrite all 45 manifests and DROP every field the generator neither produces nor carries: `carried` is exactly `managerOwnedFields` (PackageJson.ts:874, PackageJsonTemplate.ts:85-97), the manager-owned dependency blocks. Lost on first write: `smthrs` (45/45 — the very field D6 and D10 both derive tiers from), homepage and repository with per-package `directory` (43), bugs (43), tags and keywords (42), `private` (2), `bin` (2), the `./*` and `./internal/*: null` exports subpath maps, the 9-entry files list, and `publishConfig.exports`. The macro also hardcodes `@smthrs/${basename}` and `version: "0.1.0"`. Widen `carried` to preserve all of the above BEFORE generating anything, and derive `repository.directory` from the declaring package path rather than the shared template, which cannot express a per-package value. (2) `publishFields` (:403-441) emits a shape incompatible with this repo: dist-first exports with only `"."` and `"./package.json"`, no source-first form, no `publishConfig.exports`, and `files: [outDir, "README.md"]`. Either teach it the source-first plus publishConfig duality this repo actually uses, or flip the repo to dist-first — the latter conflicts with the Effect source-first convention CONTRIBUTING.md:17 mandates, so prefer the former. `Options.version` (:1176-1191) is documented as literal-only and awaiting a versioning source. (3) VERSIONING IS ALREADY SOLVED AND D10 DOES NOT SAY SO. scripts/set-release-version.mjs:45-76 already implements exactly Nx's `updateDependents: auto` across all four dependency fields, with `workspace:` and `catalog:` protocol ranges correctly excluded, and it is CI-gated at ci.yml:71. Preserve, do not reimplement — and preserve the deliberate asymmetry that it retargets ALL four groups while pack-release publishes only `engine`, because that asymmetry is what keeps the workspace resolvable after a bump. (4) What must survive any move of pack-release.mjs into the graph: the `smthrs.group` filter and the throw on an unknown group (:39-42); the topological order with alphabetical tiebreak AND the deliberate cycle-entry rule (:93-111) — the graph is NOT acyclic and `kernel -> platform-browser` is pinned by scripts/pack-release.test.mjs:125-140, so a planner that refuses cycles outright cannot order this workspace; `assertBuilt` (:164-174); the `publicationManifest` export rewrite (:137-151); and the `--list`/`--names` CLI the runbook depends on (docs/release-runbook.md:23, :98, :111-112). (5) release.yml pins that will break under restructuring: scripts/release-rehearsal.test.mjs requires exactly two `if:`-carrying steps in a fixed order (:142-151), `PACK_DIR`/`PUBLISH_ORDER` at step scope not job scope (:133-140), and a `localEquivalents` entry in release-rehearsal.mjs:366-373 for every `uses:` (:153-160). (6) Three things in release.yml cannot move into the graph and must stay hand-written: the `RELEASE_TAG`/`DRY_RUN` expression pair (:36-41), `environment: npm-publish` with `id-token: write` (:31-34), and the two mutually-exclusive `if:`-guarded terminal steps (:150, :170).

decisions: D13: any folder with a BUILD.ts is a buildable, cacheable unit
lanes.task: Build the half of D13 that does not exist, and stop rebuilding the half that does. WHAT ALREADY WORKS, verified by running the CLI against a scratch workspace: `//packages/engine/src/internal:lib` resolves today; `normalizePackage` accepts arbitrary depth (Label.ts:25-62), `packagePathForBuild` derives the package path from the BUILD.ts dirname (Workspace.ts:752-755), `packageTargets` only asks whether `<path>/BUILD.ts` is in buildFiles (:1117-1128), and the discovery filter keeps every file ending in `/BUILD.ts` regardless of depth (:794). `lint/BUILD.ts` is a live example of a BUILD.ts in a directory with no package.json. Bazel's subpackage rule for globs is also already implemented (Input.ts:401-415, :474-491, :539, :645). A nested BUILD.ts does NOT opt its parent out of default synthesis, because `eligible` checks `<directory>/BUILD.ts` only (Workspace.ts:1014-1019) — so folder units are naturally additive, which is exactly what D13's zero-boilerplate promise needs. Do not reimplement any of this. WHAT IS MISSING, and is this lane's actual work: (1) Synthesis for marker-less directories. `synthesizedDirectories` (:1066-1077) enumerates only directories containing the marker file (`package.json` by default), so a folder without one is never synthesized and `packageTargets` fails with 'has no BUILD.ts and matches no default target'. Make `marker` optional in PackageDefaults (:71-77) or add a second declaration kind. (2) Cross-unit manifest naming. The resolver installed by `synthesizeDirectory` (:1036-1048) throws for any target the macro did not just produce, so a folder unit's manifest cannot name its parent package's lib and vice versa. Relax it deliberately or accept that folder units get no manifest scripts. (3) The unit manifest shape. A `{"type":"module", "exports": ...}` resolution stub is NOT expressible today: PackageJson requires a publishable npm name (`assertPackageName`, :294-308) and a literal semver version (`assertVersion`, :227-238), and `publishFields` requires a build target with outDir and format. PackageJson.ts is owned by W5-A this wave — do not edit it. File the required shape as a cross-lane contract with W5-A and consume what it provides. (4) Fix the correction to D13's headline claim while you are in the docs: 'PackageDefaults + StandardPackage = 0 files' is not literally true. The repo has 8 BUILD.ts files (root, lint, and six under packages/), and 39 of 45 packages have none. The honest claim is zero build files for 87% of packages. Note also that every one of the 45 still hand-writes six per-package config files — package.json, tsconfig.json, tsconfig.test.json, vitest.config.ts, eslint.config.js, dprint.json, 270 files — so the property is about build-tool config only. (5) Close the scaffold gap: NewPackage writes five files (:166-210) but never tsconfig.test.json, vitest.config.ts, eslint.config.js, or dprint.json, all four of which the synthesized check/test/lint/fmt targets declare as inputs and all 45 existing packages hand-write. A missing declared file digests to undefined rather than failing (Workspace.ts:1300-1305, SafeFs.ts:637-654), so today the gap surfaces as a tool error at execution rather than a plan error. (6) COVERAGE GAP worth recording: apps/server, apps/shared, apps/tui, apps/ui, examples, and packages/build/infra all carry a package.json and are pnpm workspace members, but match no PackageDefaults glob (`directories: "packages/*"`, BUILD.ts:144) and have no BUILD.ts, so they have zero build-system targets — while root `pnpm test` does run them. Do not fix it in this lane; document it.

Update packages/targets/test/NewPackage.test.ts — 14 tests including 'creates a package a default target can pick up, with no BUILD.ts' and 'renders the same tree every time, with no model in reach' — for the four added config files. packages/build-cli/test/CommittedBuildFiles.test.ts:35-53 pins the six-target set on four named BUILD.ts files and must stay green.
